Wasa — only when the code starts with S0155 or S0118

🥔 Savoury snacks (pareve) — Amica Chips (plain and crinkle-cut crisps, ketchup, eldorada, crostino, salted popcorn, corn tortilla) — Rav A. Luzzi · San Carlo "Classiche" and "Rustiche" — BDM/BDR approved (only from the Novara plant)

🥣 Kellogg's breakfast cereals — symbol on pack: MK Manchester Beth Din or NWK North West Kosher
Corn Flakes · Rice Krispies · Special K · Frosties · Froot Loops · Coco Pops · All Bran · Miel Pops · Oaties · Extra · W.K. Kellogg granola
## Something else useful

🔬 The list of forbidden food additives — at the end of the booklet there is a table by Rabbi Riccardo Di Segni, by European E numbers: which additives are always forbidden and which are forbidden without supervision. Useful when a product is not on the list and you want to read the label.
Always forbidden: E120, E441, E542, E630, E631, E635, E1000 · may be of dairy origin: E469, E637, E966
⚠️ The list is updated every year and during it too. It is meant for private use according to each person's level of kashrut, and does not replace asking a rabbi.
kosher.milan_shuls_note:
Most of the kosher food and lodging is in the south-western quarter (Soderini · Sally Mayer · Montecuccoli · San Gimignano), and most of the synagogues too. Milan has no eruv, so the distance from your lodging to the synagogue matters.
The city has more small oratories — Centro Modena on Via Tenca and Josef Tehillot on Via dei Gracchi among others. The full list is on the community's website, mosaico-cem.it.

beginner.desc: The main blue run back to the village. It comes down from Plan Maison to Cervinia itself, and it is how most skiers get home at the end of the day.
beginner.tip: 💡 Busy around closing time. If you're not in a hurry, come down later and enjoy an empty run

beginner.desc: The blue under the Cretaz lift, which leaves from the edge of the village and climbs to Plan Torrette. A comfortable run for a first morning, and the lift brings you straight back to it.
The village nursery slope, at the foot of the Campetto lift and the Campetto magic carpet. This is where you stand on skis for the first time.
beginner.tip: 📍 At the entrance to the village. Note: Campetto is the name of the lift, not of a run

beginner.desc: Two very short blues up high, near Plan Maison. The step after the village nursery slope — the same comfort, but with the view of the high mountain.
A wide blue in the Rocce Nere area above Plan Maison. One of the two runs that reach the Chalet Etoile restaurant.
A high blue above Plan Maison, at an altitude usually kept for harder runs. Good snow even when it is already soft lower down.

beginner.area: From the shoulder below Alpe Giomein to Plan Torrette
beginner.desc: The long blue of the Plan Torrette sector: it runs from the shoulder below Alpe Giomein to the Plan Torrette junction, where the Cretaz lift ends. A wide, well-groomed slope with a gentle gradient and no steep sections — exactly what you want once you've finished with the village nursery slope and are looking for a first long run. The lift takes you back to the top, so you can do whole loops on it without going down to the village.
beginner.tip: 💡 One of the longer blues in the area, and away from the rush back to the village on run 5

beginner.area: In the Alpe Giomein area, above Plan Torrette
beginner.desc: A short blue link in the Alpe Giomein area, the continuation of red 29BIS further down. It is a connection, not a destination: its job is to take you from the upper shoulder to the Plan Torrette network, not to be skied again and again. Don't plan a day around it.
beginner.tip: 📍 Alpe Giomein is the name of the place, not of a lift — the lift that came up here from Plan Torrette was removed, and you arrive from above

intermediate.area: Plateau Rosà 3,480 m → village ~2,050 m
intermediate.desc: Cervinia's famous run, and one of the longest in the Alps. It comes down from the glacier at Plateau Rosà to the village — a descent of about 1,475 m in one go, with the Matterhorn in front of you almost all the way. The official register splits it into three sections: glacier, Goillet and Bardoney.
intermediate.tip:
📏 Sources disagree on the length: the regional register and dovesciare say 11 km, the Italian Wikipedia 8.5. The altitudes, on the other hand, are agreed
🗺️ On the map it appears as three consecutive sections: Ventina Ghiacciaio at the top, then Ventina Goillet and then Ventina Bardoney

intermediate.area: From the Ventina to the Cielo Alto district
intermediate.desc: Branches off the Ventina and comes down to the Cielo Alto district. Its section was recently eased to about 20% when run 34 was built, which passes under it in a tunnel.
intermediate.tip: 🏘️ If you stay in Cielo Alto, this is your run home

intermediate.area: Cielo Alto → village
intermediate.desc: The descent from the Cielo Alto district to the village. According to the official document it ends below the district, and until run 34 was built it was the only way back to the main lifts.

A new run, and one of the few for which the resort publishes a length and altitudes. It was built to free Cielo Alto from depending on run 16: it leaves run 21, passes through a tunnel under run 13, and joins the last section of the Ventina.
intermediate.tip: 🆕 Its steep section reaches 47% — not an "easy red" all the way

intermediate.area: Pancheron lift 2,438 → 2,949 m
intermediate.desc: The red under the six-seater Pancheron chairlift. Until 2010 it was marked black; today the area's black is 24BI beside it.

intermediate.area: Bontadini lift 3,041 → 3,332 m
intermediate.desc: Two reds on the upper part of the glacier, near the Bontadini lift. Usually the first to open in the season — in November 2025 they opened on the 7th, before everything else.
intermediate.tip: ❄️ Glacier snow. You ski here when there isn't enough lower down yet

intermediate.area: From the border pass → Plan Maison
intermediate.desc: The descent from the Colle del Teodulo, the historic border pass, back to Plan Maison. It is the comfortable way back to Italy after a day on the Swiss side.
intermediate.tip: 🇨🇭 Check the time of the last lift before you cross — see the Zermatt section

intermediate.area: Branch off the Ventina
intermediate.desc: Branches off the Ventina towards the Cime Bianche col. This is the link that connects the Cervinia area with Valtournenche and the Reine Blanche.
intermediate.tip: 🔗 The way over to the Valtournenche side

intermediate.area: Lower Cime Bianche col → Valtournenche 1,562 m
intermediate.desc: The Gran Pista of Valtournenche, run no. 1 — and a red, not a black. It has had snowmaking since 2008, and since then it has been reliable from December to April. Joined to the sections above it from Plateau Rosà, it makes a continuous descent marketed as about 22 km.
intermediate.tip: 🚌 The descent ends in Valtournenche, not Cervinia — you will need a taxi or shuttle back

intermediate.area: From the Rocce Bianche shoulder to the Gran Roc area
intermediate.desc: A long, beautiful red from the Rocce Bianche shoulder, one of the higher parts of the Italian side, down to the Gran Roc area. A continuous descent across open ground above the tree line, with the Matterhorn ridge on one side and the Breuil valley on the other. For a confident intermediate it is one of the most rewarding reds here, and at the bottom it joins red 11, which continues to Pré de Veau.
intermediate.tip: ⚠️ High, open ground — on a windy day or in poor visibility you feel it here first

intermediate.area: The upper section of Alpe Giomein
intermediate.desc: The upper section of the Alpe Giomein pair: a short red from the shoulder down to the top of blue 10. It is a link, not a run you come for — but it is the natural way on down for anyone coming from Rocce Bianche. In the official operating register it appears under the short name ALPE1 ALTA.

intermediate.area: From the Gran Roc area to the Pré de Veau junction
intermediate.desc: A short red link from the Gran Roc area to the Pré de Veau junction, where it meets the main axis down to the village. Its job is to carry whoever came down from Rocce Bianche on to the rest of the descent — there is no point planning it as a destination in itself.
intermediate.tip: 🗺️ In the official register the name is shortened to GRANR-PREDEVE, and OpenStreetMap resolves it to Gran Roc – Pré de Veau

intermediate.area: From Plan Torrette to Pré de Veau
intermediate.desc: The first link in the red chain that connects Plan Torrette with the village. It runs from the junction where the Cretaz lift arrives down to Pré de Veau: a worked, well-snowed slope with no steep sections. This is the section that starts the descent home at the end of the day.
intermediate.tip: 🗺️ On the map it appears as one line with 3.0. The official register splits the descent into numbers, but in OpenStreetMap — and so in Mapy too — it is one continuous trail called Plan Torrette-Pre de Veau. So both buttons lead to the same line.

intermediate.area: From Pré de Veau to the Pirovano and Giomein area
intermediate.desc: The direct continuation of 3. It takes you from Pré de Veau down to the Pirovano area, and ends at the edge of the village near via Giomein — a district of Cervinia in its own right, neither the village centre nor Cielo Alto.
intermediate.tip:
🗺️ It has no separate object on the map. It is marked on the same trail as 3, so the button opens the same line.
📍 Mind the name: via Giomein in the village and Alpe Giomein on the mountain are two completely different places — one is a street, the other a shoulder above Plan Torrette.

intermediate.area: From the Pirovano area to the edge of the village
intermediate.desc: The last link of the 3 chain — from the Pirovano area straight into Cervinia. A continuous red descent to the edge of the village, and the way home for everyone who started down at Plan Torrette. At closing time it is less crowded than blue 5, but also steeper — if you're not confident, take the blue.

intermediate.area: From the Pirovano area to the edge of the village
intermediate.desc: A red alternative to 3.00: it branches off at the same point in the Pirovano area, but runs down on a parallel line east of it to the edge of the village. A kilometre in one go, and usually emptier than the main axis. In the official register it appears as FALLINIERE, with no further detail.
intermediate.tip: 💡 If 3.00 is jammed at closing time — this is the parallel way down

intermediate.area: In the Bardoney sector, on the lower part of the mountain
intermediate.desc: A red of about a kilometre and a third in the Bardoney sector, on the lower part of the mountain above the village — the same area where the Ventina ends and the new link 34 passes. The descent here is below the ridgeline and relatively sheltered, so it is one of the sensible options on a day when the wind is blowing up top. It joins the axis back to the lift base.
intermediate.tip: 🌬️ Low and relatively sheltered — a good option on a windy day up top

intermediate.area: On the middle part of the mountain, between Goillet and Bardoney
intermediate.desc: A short red on the middle part of the mountain, between Goillet and Bardoney and close to the Ventina line. It is not a destination in itself but variety: if you've already done the Ventina twice, you can take it to change line within the same sector without moving area. In the official register the name Gaspard appears with no further detail.

intermediate.area: Fornet lift 2,866 → 3,048 m
intermediate.desc: A high red on the Fornet lift, at an altitude where the snow stays dry and cold even in spring. Short, but the lift takes you straight back to the top, so you can ski it again and again without losing height — a whole morning's run for anyone who likes laps. The snowpark is in the same sector, and there are no trees anywhere around: it is all open ground.
intermediate.tip: ❄️ At this altitude there is no shade and no shelter — layers and dark goggles

intermediate.area: The Furggen moraines, below the south face of the Matterhorn
intermediate.desc: A red across the glacier moraines below the south face of the Matterhorn — one of the places where the mountain looks closest in the whole area. Twelve hundred metres of open ground on a reasonable, unthreatening red gradient, ending in the Plan Maison–Pancheron sector and continuing from there to red 9. If you get one clear day in the week, save it for this run.
intermediate.tip: 📸 The view is the reason to come here; on a cloudy day it has no advantage over red 24 in the same sector

advanced.desc: The famous black of the Italian side, built in 2010 together with the Pancheron lift. The opening wall reaches about 65% and the rest of the run stays above 55%. A 250 m drop in one kilometre, and the last section merges into red 9.
advanced.tip: ⚠️ Not a "hard red". This is a real black, below the Furggen ridges

advanced.desc: The black beside red 24, on the same lift. Easy to come back to again and again without going down to the village.

advanced.area: From the top station of the Cielo Alto lift, 2,476 m
advanced.desc: Comes straight down from the top station of the Cielo Alto lift. Reshaped in the project that built run 34.
The upper black of Cielo Alto. Run 34 branches off it.
A black in the official register, with no snowmaking — so it depends on natural snow.
advanced.tip: ⚠️ The exact location is not published in any source we checked. Ask on the spot

advanced.desc: A black in the official register, with no snowmaking.
advanced.tip: ⚠️ The exact location is not published

advanced.desc: The seventh and last of Cervinia's blacks. Its name is kept from the Gran Roc lift, which was removed.
The two blacks on the Valtournenche side. Neither has snowmaking.

apres_ski.desc: The mountain's long-standing, best-known après-ski. A hut on the slope with a terrace facing the Matterhorn, a DJ and live music. Get there by cable car to Plan Maison and then run 5, or by the Cretaz lift.
apres_ski.tip: ⛷️ Skiers only — no access on foot · open from the morning, après-ski starts in the afternoon · ☎ +39 345 800 2544 · lovecervinia.com

apres_ski.area: Plan Torrette 2,450 m — at the foot of the Pancheron lift
apres_ski.desc: Opened in December 2024, part of the chain that started in Courmayeur. Over 700 m²: an igloo bar, a space for 200 people and a "beach on the snow" sun deck. House music and sunset over the Matterhorn.

apres_ski.area: Alpe Giomein — on the red run between Plan Torrette and Cretaz
apres_ski.desc: Right on the way home, which makes it a natural stop at the end of the day. A sun deck by the pool.
apres_ski.tip: ⛷️ Ski in/Ski out · the party style is described in ski guides, not on the hotel's own site

apres_ski.area: Via Bich 10 — village centre, opposite the nursery slope
apres_ski.desc: A pub since 1984, and a recognised "beer academy" since 1993. Nine taps and another 25–30 bottled beers, among them the local "4478" — named after the height of the Matterhorn. Two big screens for sport.

apres_ski.area: Via J. B. Bich 3 — in the village, about 100 m from the Cretaz lift
apres_ski.desc: A British pub inside the Chalet Hotel Dragon: karaoke, pub quizzes, sport on screens and a terrace overlooking the runs home. Next to it, Thistles — two rooms of the same house.
apres_ski.tip: 🍻 Not at Plan Maison as was once written here — it is in the village

apres_ski.desc: A lively bar on the upper floor, with a cellar space of the same name below it. Live music at times.

apres_ski.area: Piazza Guide Maquignaz 4 — near the Hotel Maquignaz
apres_ski.desc: A cocktail bar from mid-afternoon that turns into a party venue at night. On the walls, paintings by the local artist Marie Ange Maquignaz.
apres_ski.tip: 🍸 Restaurant at lunch and dinner, cocktail bar from mid-afternoon until midnight · ☎ +39 376 205 8304 (WhatsApp too) · ymeletrob.it

valtournenche.area: Salette 2,245 m → Plan de La Glaea 1,524 m
valtournenche.desc: The main run of Valtournenche, from the Salette area down to the village's valley station. This is the lower part of the long descent from the border — start at the top and this is where you end up.
valtournenche.tip: 🏘️ Ends in Valtournenche village, not Cervinia — check how you get back

valtournenche.desc: The blue at the Campetto station, at the lower end of the Valtournenche area. A comfortable run for learning.
A short blue in the Motta area, above the village.
The run back to the Valtournenche valley station. The way home at the end of the day.
A red in the Salette area, on the middle part of the mountain above Valtournenche.

valtournenche.area: In the Bec Carré area 2,420 m
valtournenche.desc: A wide blue in the Bec Carré area, named after Alberto Nussan. Part of the upper run network of Valtournenche.
A red in the upper part of the Valtournenche area, on the way down from Bec Carré.
Comes down from the Becca d'Aran station, one of the Valtournenche mid-stations.
A blue in the Roisette area, on the lower part of the mountain.

zermatt.area: 3,824 → 3,899 m · the highest point in the area
zermatt.desc: The highest point you can ski in the whole ski area, according to the lift operator. It sits on the glacier above the Klein Matterhorn and is reached by a drag lift — the highest in Europe. The slope itself is gentle.
zermatt.tip: ⚠️ The lift only runs when snow and weather allow. At 3,900 m the air is thin and much colder than lower down

zermatt.area: From the summit station 3,883 m to the glacier
zermatt.desc: The descent from Europe's highest cable car station. This is also where the longest descent in the area begins — 14.6 km to Zermatt village according to the lift operator.
zermatt.tip: 📏 3,883 m is the summit. The cable car station itself is at 3,820 m, with the viewing platform above

zermatt.area: Between Trockener Steg and the border area
zermatt.desc: The axis across the Theodul glacier. This is the run you take back and forth between the two countries, so it is also the first to feel the wind.
zermatt.tip: 💨 When the weather turns, it is sometimes closed early here — even before a lift stops

zermatt.area: At the foot of the Gandegghütte, above Trockener Steg
zermatt.desc: Comes down in the area of the Gandegghütte (3,029 m), the old hut overlooking the glacier. A natural part of the way between Trockener Steg and the border.
A wide red in the bowl above Trockener Steg, named after the Theodul lake at its foot.
Comes down from the Furggsattel saddle. The chair that serves it is the last link on the way back to Italy, and also the first to close in the wind.
zermatt.tip: ⏰ This is the run to know: its closing time decides how late you can still get back

zermatt.desc: The area's race run, wide and with an even gradient. It comes down from Trockener Steg towards Furgg.

zermatt.area: From the Furgg area to Furi
zermatt.desc: One of the reds that connect the Furgg area with Furi, on the way down to the village.
Comes down on the western side below Schwarzsee, facing the north face of the Matterhorn. A quieter side of the mountain.
The black of the Schwarzsee area, named after the Hörnli ridge from which climbers set out for the summit of the Matterhorn.
The lower part of the long descent to Zermatt, through the hamlet of Blatten above the village.
Part of the descent from the Gornergrat to the village, on the section above Furi.

zermatt.area: From the Gornergrat railway station 3,089 m
zermatt.desc: A wide blue from the mountain railway station. This area is the one to choose if you're less confident, and you can get there by train too — handy for a mixed group.
zermatt.tip: 🚂 The Gornergrat railway is not always included in the ski pass — check at the ticket office

zermatt.desc: A short blue near the Rotenboden station, on a stretch where the Matterhorn is in front of you almost the whole time.
The start of the big descent on the Swiss side: from Hohtälli via the Gornergrat to the village, about 1,600 m of almost continuous skiing.
zermatt.tip: 🌅 Best in the morning, before the sun softens the slope

zermatt.desc: Zermatt's well-known black, on the steep section above the village.
The main blue of the Sunnegga area, Zermatt's learning area. Reached by an underground funicular from the village.
zermatt.tip: 👨‍👩‍👧 Zermatt's beginner area is here too

zermatt.area: On the back side of the Rothorn
zermatt.desc: Comes down the back side of the Rothorn ridge, away from the crowds. An area that holds good snow when conditions are right.
zermatt.tip: ❄️ Worth checking whether it's open — it isn't always

zermatt.desc: A red in the eastern bowl, near the Fluhalp hut (2,616 m). From its terrace you see the whole Matterhorn.
A direct black in the Rothorn area, on the upper part of the ridge.
The longest descent in the area: from the Klein Matterhorn station via the Theodul glacier, Trockener Steg, Furgg and Furi to the village. 14.6 km according to the lift operator.
zermatt.tip: 📏 3,883 m is the summit — the cable car station is at 3,820. The highest skiable point is 3,899 m at the Gobba di Rollin

zermatt.desc: The hardest run in the whole ski area, on either side of the border. A steep descent of about 565 m between rocks.
zermatt.tip: ⚠️ There is no single blue run down to Zermatt village. If you're not confident on reds — don't go down; come back by cable car

restaurants.piste: Plateau Rosà — at the cable car station
restaurants.desc: The highest mountain hut in the area, right at the top station of the cable car to Plateau Rosà. It belongs to the Matterhorn guides' association. The Ventina starts here, and this is where you cross to Zermatt.

restaurants.piste: At the top station of the Bontadini lift
restaurants.desc: An Italian Alpine Club mountain hut on the historic border pass, with panoramic windows onto the Matterhorn and the Grandes Murailles. The regional register lists 10 rooms for overnight stays.

restaurants.piste: On run 6, at the foot of the Bontadini lift
restaurants.desc: One of the oldest on Cervinia's slopes, with one of the biggest panoramic terraces in the area. You can also walk up in snowshoes from Plan Maison.
restaurants.tip: ☎ +39 335 250 312 · dogs welcome · full-moon evenings with a ski descent

restaurants.piste: On run 7, the Ventina
restaurants.desc: The big hut on the Ventina, on the section between Plateau Rosà and the Cime Bianche col. 150 seats inside and another 30 outside, with deckchairs.

restaurants.piste: On the Ventina, at the foot of the Gran Sometta lift
restaurants.desc: A small baita with a sun-drenched terrace facing the Matterhorn. The natural stop for anyone crossing between Valtournenche and Cervinia. Since 2023 an "Ice Lodge" — an igloo and ice bar — goes up there in December.

restaurants.piste: Runs 6 and 26, above Plan Maison
restaurants.area: Loc. Rocce Nere — Plan Maison, ~2,750 m
restaurants.desc: The most famous of the huts, run by the Frassy family since 1974 — Cesare Frassy opened it, and today his children run it. 80 seats inside and 150 outside, with a large sun terrace.

restaurants.piste: Plan Maison — next to the cable car station
restaurants.desc: Less than a hundred metres from the cable car exit. You can get there without skis too — handy if you came up just for the view.

restaurants.piste: Inside the Cime Bianche Laghi cable car station
restaurants.desc: A tavola calda inside the cable car station itself. 70 seats, all on the terrace, facing the Matterhorn.
restaurants.tip: ☎ +39 348 494 2442 · ⚠️ not to be confused with the "Cime Bianche" hotel down in the valley — two different places

restaurants.piste: On run 7, the Ventina, in the Bardoney area
restaurants.desc: A wooden hut from 1983, renovated in 2012, on the lower part of the Ventina. 45 seats inside and 90 outside, with views of the Matterhorn and the Grandes Murailles.
restaurants.tip: ☎ +39 389 194 3622 · igloocervinia.com · in the evening — booking required

restaurants.piste: Where the Ventina ends
restaurants.desc: Sits exactly at the point where runs 7, 34 and 3bis arrive — in other words, the last stop of the day. 100 seats.

restaurants.piste: At the foot of the Cretaz run, near the Campetto lift
restaurants.area: Loc. Campetto 1 — edge of the village
restaurants.desc: A hut-hotel at the edge of the village, with a large terrace facing the Matterhorn. 100 seats inside and 200 outside.
restaurants.tip: ☎ +39 0166 949914 · hotelbaitacretaz.com · in winter they pick guests up by snowmobile

restaurants.piste: ⚠️ Not on a run — near the Lago Blu lake
restaurants.area: Lago Blu ~1,980 m, below the village
restaurants.desc: A family place by the blue lake. You can't ski there and no lift goes there — drive or take a taxi, or walk about half an hour from the village.
restaurants.tip: ☎ +39 0166 949398 · alpage-cervinia.com · snow chains may be needed in winter

restaurants.piste: On run 73, on the way between Trockener Steg and the border
restaurants.desc: An old hut on the edge of the Theodul glacier, with a terrace facing the glacier and the Matterhorn. The natural place to stop on the way to or from the pass.

restaurants.piste: In the hamlet of Findeln, below Sunnegga
restaurants.desc: The most famous hut in Zermatt, in the Alpine hamlet of Findeln below Sunnegga. A terrace with a direct view of the Matterhorn.
restaurants.tip: 📞 Tables are taken in advance — especially at lunchtime

restaurants.piste: In the hamlet of Findeln, next to Chez Vrony
restaurants.desc: Chez Vrony's neighbour in the same hamlet, a terrace with the same view and usually less crowded.

restaurants.piste: On run 19, in the eastern bowl
restaurants.desc: A mountain hut in the bowl below Blauherd, with one of the best-known terraces in the area facing the Matterhorn.

restaurants.piste: At the Schwarzsee station
restaurants.desc: Right at the foot of the Matterhorn, by the small lake that gives the station its name. The meeting point of the runs going down to Furi.

restaurants.piste: On the way from Furi to the village
restaurants.desc: Zermatt's well-known après-ski bar, right on the run on the last stretch down to the village. Opens in the afternoon.
restaurants.tip: ⏰ If you stop here, you're not getting back to Italy that day

restaurants.piste: On the Gran Pista, above Valtournenche
restaurants.desc: A hut on the main run of Valtournenche, on the way down to the village.

restaurants.piste: In the Motta area, Valtournenche
restaurants.desc: Near the Motta mid-station, in the heart of the Valtournenche ski area.

restaurants.piste: On run 3 on the Chantorné plateau
restaurants.desc: The main hut of the Torgnon plateau, right on the run that bears its name.

restaurants.piste: On the upper part of the Chantorné plateau
restaurants.desc: A higher alpage on the plateau, towards the Collet chairlift.

restaurants.piste: Above Chamois village
restaurants.desc: A mountain hut above the village of Chamois, a village with no road to it.

restaurants.piste: Near Lago Lod
restaurants.desc: On the shore of Lake Lod, near the Chamois nursery slope.

nearby.desc: The main descent of Torgnon, from the Chantorné plateau to the village of Mongnod.
The main blue of the Chantorné plateau — Torgnon's central slope.
Another blue on the plateau, near the Des Troncs restaurant that gives it its name.

nearby.area: From the top of the Collet chairlift 2,246 m
nearby.desc: Comes down from the top station of the Collet chairlift, the high part of Torgnon.
A red on the wooded section of the mountain, in the upper part of Torgnon.

nearby.area: On the western side of the plateau
nearby.desc: A red on the western side of the Chantorné plateau.
A red named after Piergiorgio Grange, in the western part of the area.
A red in the upper area of the plateau.
The main run of Chamois, coming down to the village itself.
A variant of the Assetaz, on the same slope.
The Chamois nursery slope, near Lake Lod. A run for real first-timers.

routes.title: The grand tour — Plan Maison, Bontadini and back to Cretaz
routes.summary: A few hours of skiing without a single hard run, with beautiful huts along the way worth stopping at. There are two completely different ways to reach Plan Maison — one gives you a warm-up of two long blues, the other takes you straight up. From Plan Maison on the route is the same: three chairlifts up to the Bontadini ridge, and a descent that starts as an easy red and continues blue all the way to Cretaz.

legs.name: Two ways to reach Plan Maison

options.label: A. The gondola from the village
options.text: Straight up, with no skiing on the way. The quick way — good if you set off late or want to get up high fast.

options.label: B. <bdi dir="ltr">Cretaz → Pancheron</bdi>, with a warm-up
options.text: Two chairlifts to the top of Pancheron, then two long blues (26 and then 6.00) down to Plan Maison. About 4.5 km of warm-up before you start in earnest.

routes.title: The Ventina — one descent from the summit to the village
routes.summary: Cervinia's famous descent: 7.6 km in one go and a 1,430 m drop, from Plateau Rosa at 3,480 m to the gondola station in the village. Red all the way, but wide and even — more long than hard. From Plan Maison you go up in two gondolas.

stats.time: Two hours or more · about an hour non-stop
